defects.description: The completeness check that detects an unresolved cycle uses `>`, but the emitted order can never exceed the node count, so the branch is never taken and `topo_sort` silently returns a partial ordering for cyclic graphs instead of raising CycleError.
paraphrases: Comparing the produced-order length with strictly-greater-than can only ever be false, so a graph containing a cycle yields a truncated result and no exception is thrown.
Because the number of ordered nodes is at most the number of nodes, the guard's `>` condition is unreachable, and unschedulable graphs are accepted rather than reported as cyclic.
The cycle-detection gate should fire whenever fewer nodes were ordered than exist; using greater-than means it never fires, letting cyclic input pass through as an incomplete list.

defects.description: Cycle detection tests for a BLACK (finished) neighbor instead of a GRAY (on-stack) one, so genuine back-edges into the active DFS path are missed and `find_cycle` returns None for cyclic graphs while spuriously flagging some acyclic ones.
paraphrases: The DFS looks for an edge into an already-completed node rather than one into a node still on the recursion stack, which fails to recognize the back-edge that constitutes a real cycle.

Detecting the loop requires spotting a neighbor currently colored in-progress; checking for the finished color instead lets true cycles slip by undetected and can misread cross-edges in a DAG as loops.
By keying on the terminal color, the traversal no longer identifies revisits to the active path, so it reports no cycle where one exists.

defects.anchor: depth[node] = max(depth[dep] for dep in node_deps)
defects.correct_form: depth[node] = 1 + max(depth[dep] for dep in node_deps)
defects.description: A dependent node's level is set to the maximum of its dependencies' levels without adding one, so the longest-chain depth never grows and every node collapses to level 0 instead of being one deeper than its prerequisites.
paraphrases: The recurrence omits the `+1` step, so a node inherits its deepest dependency's level verbatim and the whole graph flattens to a single depth.
Level assignment fails to advance past its dependencies: taking the max without incrementing means chains of prerequisites all resolve to the same value.
Because the depth is not raised above its inputs, nodes that should sit progressively deeper than their dependencies all land at level zero.

defects.description: The level buckets are allocated with `range(span)` rather than `range(span + 1)`, leaving no slot for the deepest level, so `group_by_level` raises IndexError when a node occupies the maximum level.
paraphrases: Levels run from 0 through the maximum inclusive, but only that many buckets minus one are created, so indexing the top level overruns the list.
The bucket list is one entry short of the needed count; a node whose level equals the span has nowhere to go and the append blows past the end of the array.
Sizing the staging containers to the span instead of span-plus-one omits the final level's slot, triggering an out-of-range write for the deepest nodes.

gray_zones.note: `_sort_key` orders nodes by the repr of `(type(node).__name__, str(node))`, so heterogeneous or numeric nodes are compared as strings and sort lexicographically (e.g. '10' before '9'); a reviewer might flag this as a surprising, non-numeric tie-break. It is not one of the injected defects.
